entry.title: feat(reader): open a word by tapping and its sentence by holding the …
entry.content:
feat(reader): open a word by tapping and its sentence by holding the line

The double tap carried two meanings resolved after the fact, and the scroll that
kept a sheet clear of the tapped word cancelled the gesture that same tap had
begun. A tap is now answered by whatever it landed on, and a 450ms press opens
sentence details while the finger is still down. Repeats on touch are inert;
mouse and keyboard behaviour is unchanged.

The reading surface gives up native selection and the platform callout under a
finger only, because that press is now the application's gesture. Details are
quieter with it: an icon route to the sentence, grammar always readable, sheets
capped at half the viewport with the handle and action tray always reachable,
and anchored cards closing from their own corner. See ADR 0057.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: fix(vocabulary): align the standing line and stop it contradicting th…
entry.content:
fix(vocabulary): align the standing line and stop it contradicting the list

The count and its detail are two type sizes on one line, and the flex row that
holds them never set a baseline, so the smaller half rode high against the bold
number.

With no sources at all the same line read "0 words · from an unrecorded source"
while the row underneath said there were none. Removing the last source leaves
an empty snapshot behind, which is the standing of a fresh install; it says so.
A snapshot that still has words keeps its count whatever the list shows.

entry.title: feat(vocabulary): one Anki entry, a list, and a page per source
entry.content:
feat(vocabulary): one Anki entry, a list, and a page per source

The Words section asked a question the learner could not answer — "Anki" or
"AnkiDroid bridge", when the device decides which can work — and asked for the
AnkiConnect port before anything had failed. Every setting a source has lived in
its list row, so four sources were four stacked control panels and no list.

The platform is now a port, decided once at the shell edge, so one Anki entry
picks its own adapter and its own copy; iOS says plainly that a file is its only
route. A row carries the name, where the words came from and how many, and opens
a page where the settings are ordered by how often each is touched. Failures are
told in the sheet the learner pressed Anki in, each with the one link that
unblocks it and its code beside the doc keyed by those codes. The port moved
there, behind a fold, next to the retry it changes.

No stored data changes shape.

entry.title: feat(vocabulary): let Android connect to Anki through the bridge
entry.content:
feat(vocabulary): let Android connect to Anki through the bridge

Provider selection and the connection draft both hardcoded 'desktop-connect', so
the Android adapter was unreachable and mobile users silently probed the desktop
one. Carries the provider kind through selection, draft and persistence, gives the
bridge its own setup panel, names it apart from desktop Anki in the source list,
implements sampleFields so auto-suggest works, and renders the capability
limitations that were being collected and dropped. An unrecognised remote error
after a successful version handshake now reads as unsupported-action rather than
advising a permission setting that does not exist.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: feat(anki): ship a first-party read-only AnkiDroid bridge
entry.content:
feat(anki): ship a first-party read-only AnkiDroid bridge

AnkiconnectAndroid omits requestPermission, findCards and cardsInfo, returns an
unparseable envelope for unknown actions, and skips the private-network preflight
header, so Anki vocabulary could never sync on Android. Adds a small Kotlin app in
android-bridge/ that serves the eight allowed AnkiConnect reads over loopback from
AnkiDroid's public ContentProvider, read-only by construction through an allowlist
router. protocol/ holds the wire contract and the golden fixtures both sides test
against. The web artifact and its deployment are unchanged; the APK has its own
gate, its own bridge-v* release lane, and its own resolved-licence check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: refactor(repo): give the web app its own directory
entry.content:
refactor(repo): give the web app its own directory

Move the Angular app, its scripts, configs, and node_modules into web/, so
root holds only what spans the system (docs, CI, the android bridge and
protocol coming next) and web/ holds everything of its own. Keep
scripts/docs/verify-decision-index.mjs and scripts/licenses/check-licenses.mjs
at root since docs/ stays at root. Add a thin root package.json that forwards
every documented command via npm --prefix web, split .prettierignore so
formatting still runs over the whole tree from root while linting stays
web-scoped, and re-anchor .gitignore, CI composite actions, workflow artifact
paths, dependabot, and relative doc/source links to the new layout.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: feat(generation): let an empty premise ask for a topic of its own
entry.content:
feat(generation): let an empty premise ask for a topic of its own

Leaving the premise empty now generates rather than blocking the button. The absence has to reach
the model as an instruction: the story and blueprint prompts say that no premise was supplied and
that the model chooses one concrete everyday situation, because an empty data block would arrive as
a premise that says nothing. Repair and segment prompts, which revise a story that already exists,
omit the block instead, and a story saved without a premise passes none on as translation context.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: fix(reader): open a word on the tap that asked for it
entry.content:
fix(reader): open a word on the tap that asked for it

A first touch word tap was held for the sentence gesture window and only then replayed, so every
ordinary word tap on a phone arrived late enough to feel unanswered and readers learned to tap
twice. The tap now activates the word immediately; the paragraph remembers where it landed instead
of holding its click, and a second tap in the same sentence still opens sentence details while
consuming the click that would otherwise put the word away.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: refactor(reader): give the reader's selection a store of its own
entry.content:
refactor(reader): give the reader's selection a store of its own

A sentence is opened by press, by double tap, or from a focused word, and a word
by press or by keyboard — but once open, the four things that can be asked for
are the same four every time, and each has to re-read the reading's summaries
afterwards. That was in the component beside the code deciding where a popover
goes. Only the placement is about the page.

The last of the three seams the debt register named. The reader page is now
1,481 lines and 14 injected dependencies, down from 1,675 and 22, and what is
left in it is mostly one concern: measurement and placement. No behaviour
changes; the unit suite, the full browser lane, and the PWA suite all pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: refactor(reader): give the aids lane a store of its own
entry.content:
refactor(reader): give the aids lane a store of its own

The reader page held five collaborators to answer one question per aid — the
whole-reading translation job, the preparation lane, the text model's readiness,
the voice's readiness, and whether there is a network — plus the two failure
strings a stop can produce, and the order a stop has to happen in for the lane
not to pick the layer up again. None of that is about the page.

What is left there is the projection: turning a reading, a progress, a readiness,
and a connection into the row the Story options menu draws.

The second of the three seams. No behaviour changes: 1,576 lines and 18
dependencies become 1,536 and 13.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: refactor(reader): give the reading's audio a store of its own
entry.content:
refactor(reader): give the reading's audio a store of its own

The reader page wired five audio collaborators — the generation job,
application-wide playback, this reading's clip maintenance, the voice settings,
and the configuration a request is gated on — alongside two unrelated concerns.
They are now one store, provided by the reader so the player's open state dies
with the screen while playback outlives it. The page keeps what is about the
page: the player's measured height and the confirmation before clips go.

The first of the three seams the debt register names. No behaviour changes:
1,675 lines and 22 dependencies become 1,576 and 18.

entry.title: docs(repo): make the guide and the registers match the application
entry.content:
docs(repo): make the guide and the registers match the application

Help omitted pasted lists from the one paragraph about word sources, called the
sentence gesture a long press after it became a double tap, and described marked
words in Anki's terms on a screen a pasted list also reaches. The 50-word floor
is now read from the rule it states, so the three surfaces that say it cannot
disagree again.

The debt register named the generation store as the largest unit; it is fifth.
The reader page and its two largest collaborators are now recorded instead, with
the seams to extract along.

The chapter 9 index listed 54 of 56 records, and one of the missing two was
linked from another record's amendment note. A check that every decision file
appears there now runs in `verify:static` and in CI's static job, which `gate`
already requires. It found the second gap on its first run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: fix(repo): put the interface back on one measure and one vocabulary
entry.content:
fix(repo): put the interface back on one measure and one vocabulary

Measured at 1280px, the shelf overhung the app bar by 80px on both sides and
Help indented 121px past the wordmark, because two pages set a measure of their
own. Both now use the shared rail; Help keeps its prose readable by holding its
paragraphs rather than its page. Deep-linked sections carry enough scroll margin
that the page they landed on is still named above them.

A disabled button was only dimmed, which reads as greyed out over a dark green
fill and as the loudest thing on the screen over a light sage one, so it now
takes the sunken surface and secondary text in both themes. Cards stopped
stretching to their neighbour's height. An open pasted-list editor no longer
draws over the Words heading it was refused a row below. Settings rendered one
fact list three ways and one small-caps label seven ways: each is now defined
once, and the design system says when the capitals are allowed.

Deletion dialogs stored capitalised phrases and joined them mid-sentence. The
phrases are lowercase and the sentence is built at render time, in the words the
rest of the application uses.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: feat(reading): rename a story and unify what a dead link looks like
entry.content:
feat(reading): rename a story and unify what a dead link looks like

A pasted reading is titled with its own first sentence, and nothing could change
that afterwards: the title and the opening words stayed the same string, and a
model-titled story was permanent. Rename now sits in the library card's overflow
menu — which held one item and needed opening to reveal it — writing only the
title through the reading repository, and the shelf shows the new name without
re-reading the page a learner has scrolled.

Three routes could conclude a link addresses nothing, and each looked like a
different application: one landed on a bare card with no app identity at all,
two shared a full-width outlined button used nowhere else. They now render one
panel with the ordinary action pair. The shell also drops its masthead only for
the reader itself, decided by classifying the id rather than by matching the
`/reader/` prefix, so a link that names no reading keeps a way out of the app.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: fix(reader): make the reading text traversable by keyboard
entry.content:
fix(reader): make the reading text traversable by keyboard

A long story put a tab stop on every word, so hundreds of stops separated the
header from anything after the text. Each sentence now holds one stop; arrow
keys move between its words, Home and End reach its ends, and the last word
focused there becomes the sentence's stop. A skip link reaches the Library
action past the story, and story titles carry Japanese language metadata in the
Library card and the reader header.

Focus only: nothing here observes a pointer, so touch selection and the sentence
double tap are unchanged.
